## Overview

This integration brings into Gladys the **marine weather of [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com)** at up to five spots of your choice, anywhere in the world: a surf break, a harbour, a sailing area, a kitesurf beach. For each spot you get the **waves** (significant height, period, direction), the **swell** and the **wind sea**, the **water temperature**, the **ocean current**, the **sea level** with the tides, the **wind** and its gusts, plus the **Beaufort force** and the **Douglas sea state** worked out by the integration. Each spot becomes a device to show on a dashboard and to use in scenes.

Open-Meteo builds these data from the wave, ocean and weather models of national weather services (Météo-France, ECMWF, DWD, NOAA…). No account and no key are needed: the free API is for **non-commercial use**, fewer than 10,000 calls a day. [Weather data by Open-Meteo.com](https://open-meteo.com/), under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). This community integration is not affiliated with Open-Meteo.

> **These are model forecasts, not observations, and they are not fit for the safety of navigation.** The accuracy near the coast is limited. Before going to sea, read the official marine forecast of your weather service.

It is a **cloud** integration: it reads each spot every 15 or 30 minutes with two requests (marine data, then wind) and keeps the 7-day forecasts in `/data`, so a restart costs no request.

## Prerequisites

- Gladys Assistant 5.3.0 or later.
- Access to the internet from Gladys.
- The coordinates of your spots, **at sea**.

## Configuration

| Field                           | What to type                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Spot 1 … 5: name                | The name shown in the device and the widgets, for example "Quiberon". Optional.                       |
| Spot 1 … 5: latitude, longitude | Decimal degrees, `47.45, -3.20` (a decimal comma works with a space: `47,45 -3,20`). Spot 1 required. |
| Reading interval                | 15 or 30 minutes (default 30): the models are updated a few times a day.                              |
| Wind unit                       | Knots (default), km/h or m/s, in the widgets and the scene texts.                                     |
| Language of the texts           | Device names and scene summaries. Automatic: the language of your dashboard.                          |

**Place the point at sea**, a few km off the coast where the waves come in: right-click on the sea in Google Maps (or OpenStreetMap) and copy the coordinates. Open-Meteo takes the nearest sea cell of its wave models, 5 to 25 km wide, so a point on the beach usually works too. A point inland gets no marine data: the integration refuses it and says so at the top of the page.

Save: the status at the top of the page shows each spot, its sea state now and the time of the next reading. **Read now** reads again at once, a spot refused as inland included (not again within five minutes when the data are fresh). **Diagnostic** writes the state of the integration to the Logs tab.

## Usage

### Devices

In the **Discover** tab, create the "Marine weather …" device of each spot. It holds 15 features:

| Feature                          | Unit          | Note                                              |
| -------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Wave height, period, direction   | m, s, degrees | significant height; direction the waves come from |
| Swell height, period, direction  | m, s, degrees | waves born far away                               |
| Wind sea height                  | m             | waves raised by the local wind                    |
| Water temperature                | °C            | sea surface; kept out of the room temperature     |
| Current speed                    | km/h          | not available in every sea                        |
| Sea level                        | m             | above the global mean sea level, tides included   |
| Mean wind, gusts, wind direction | km/h, degrees | at 10 m; Gladys has no knot unit                  |
| Beaufort force                   | 0 … 12        | from the mean wind (WMO bounds in knots)          |
| Sea state (Douglas)              | 0 … 9         | from the significant wave height                  |

Douglas sea state: 0 calm (glassy), 1 calm (rippled) up to 0.1 m, 2 smooth up to 0.5 m, 3 slight up to 1.25 m, 4 moderate up to 2.5 m, 5 rough up to 4 m, 6 very rough up to 6 m, 7 high up to 9 m, 8 very high up to 14 m, 9 phenomenal.

The values are those of the last reading while it is less than an hour old (15-minute model data), then the hourly forecast of the current hour. A value Open-Meteo does not give is not published. Renaming a spot keeps its device; moving it to other waters (about 1 km or more) makes a new device.

### Dashboard widgets

![The Sea conditions widget off Quiberon, the 72-hour charts of the waves and of the wind, and the Sea, next 7 days list (generated illustration, not a screenshot)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/William-De71/gladys-open-meteo-marine/main/docs/assets/widgets.en.png)

- **Sea conditions**: tiles for the waves, their period, the swell (and where it comes from), the water and the wind; the sea state, the Beaufort force, the gusts, the swell and the current; the navigation warning.
- **Marine forecast chart**: the next 48 or 72 hours of the waves, the swell and the wind sea (in metres), or of the mean wind and the gusts; the highest waves and the strongest wind with their time.
- **Sea, next 7 days**: day by day, the highest waves, the swell and its period, the strongest wind and its Beaufort force, and the sea state as a colored badge.

Choose the spot in the settings of the widget (empty: the first one). Each widget names its source, Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

### Scenes

Three triggers, one event per transition. The first reading of a spot is a reference and fires nothing. A value within 5 % of a bound keeps its level, so the small moves of the model fire nothing.

- **Open-Meteo Marine: sea state changed**: the Douglas sea state of a spot changes. Filter by spot and by new sea state ("rough" and above, for example).
- **Open-Meteo Marine: Beaufort force changed**: the force of the mean wind changes. Filter by spot and by new force.
- **Open-Meteo Marine: strong wind forecast**: within the next 24 hours, the forecast reaches force 7 (near gale) or more, the threshold of coastal gale warnings, or a higher force than already announced. It is announced again only after the forecast went back below force 7.

Each one gives a ready-made sentence, `{{triggerEvent.data.summary}}`, and its values (heights, periods, wind in km/h and knots…).

The **Open-Meteo Marine: read the marine forecast** action returns the sea and the wind of a spot now, or in 1 to 168 hours: waves, swell, wind sea, water, wind, gusts, Beaufort force, sea state and a summary. It reads the kept forecast and makes no request.

Examples:

- When the sea state becomes "rough" or more at the harbour → send `{{triggerEvent.data.summary}}` to the skipper.
- When a strong wind is forecast → notify, and bring the garden furniture in.
- Every Saturday at 7:00 → read the marine forecast in 3 hours; if the swell is above 1 m and its period above 10 s, send "Surf's up".

### Transport

Cloud only: the data come from `marine-api.open-meteo.com` and `api.open-meteo.com`. Only the coordinates of the spots leave your network, with a user agent naming the integration.

## Troubleshooting

- **"no marine data at this point"**: the point is on land, or in a lake or a narrow estuary the wave models do not cover. Move it a few km out to sea, save, then press **Read now**.
- **"unreadable coordinates"**: type `latitude, longitude` in decimal degrees, latitude first: `47.45, -3.20`. Degrees-minutes (47°27'N) are not read.
- **The current or the sea level stays empty**: Open-Meteo has no value for this sea. This is normal.
- **The values differ from the buoy or the official forecast**: these are model data on a grid of 5 to 25 km; near the coast they are less accurate.
- **"Open-Meteo limits the requests (HTTP 429)"**: the free quota is counted per IP address. The integration waits at least an hour. Choose 30 minutes and check that no other software on the same network calls Open-Meteo a lot.
- **"Open-Meteo is unavailable"** or **"unreachable"**: the integration tries again after 5, 10, 20 and 40 minutes; meanwhile the devices follow the hourly forecast already kept.
- **To report a problem**: press **Diagnostic**, then copy the lines starting with "Marine diagnostic" from the Logs tab into a GitHub issue or a reply on the forum. Include the versions of Gladys and of the integration.

## How to install Open-Meteo Marine in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Open-Meteo Marine appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/william-de71/gladys-open-meteo-marine:0.1.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-open-meteo-marine](https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-open-meteo-marine).

Open-Meteo Marine requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Open-Meteo Marine is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [William-De71](https://github.com/William-De71), not by the Gladys core team.
